clue.text: Ugly surroundings of square where bandits lurk

indicators.note: the ugly word forms the surroundings of the square, so it wraps around it

parts.note: ugly means hideous
a T-square is a drawing square, giving T

explanation.surface: A description of the grim landscape around a town square where outlaws hang about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings of' puts T inside HIDEOUS, between the E and the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideaways are the secret refuges where outlaws hide from the law.

clue.text: Monkey that utters long doleful cries

definitions.meaning: someone or something that howls, letting out long mournful wails

explanation.surface: A description of a monkey known for its mournful wailing.
explanation.definitionFit: The howler monkey is named for its roar; anything that wails long and loud is also so called.

clue.text: Mysterious Dickensian grabbing one-foot-wide bit of timber

indicators.note: the Dickens character grabbing the other pieces holds them inside his name

parts.note: Edwin Drood, of Dickens's unfinished The Mystery of Edwin Drood
one is the Roman numeral I
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A shadowy Dickens character snatches a narrow plank of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts IFTW inside the surname, splitting it after its first two letters. Edwin Drood is the title figure of Dickens's unfinished mystery novel, hence 'Mysterious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood washed up by the sea is a piece of timber found on a beach.

clue.text: It's a bore to lubricate properly

parts.note: to lubricate a machine is to oil it
properly means well, as in done well

explanation.surface: Someone complains that greasing a machine thoroughly is a tedious chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull task; it is a drilled shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft drilled into the ground to reach petroleum is a bore.

clue.text: The rise and fall of belief

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading the same going up as coming down means the word is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A history title tracing how a faith rose and then declined.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same upwards and downwards in the grid, so its rise and fall are identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine held to be true is a belief.

clue.text: Orders to a senior officer if cut off

indicators.note: cut off says the end of the officer's rank is lopped

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: Commands are passed to a high-ranking officer in case communications are severed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' looks like commands; it means classes or ranks of living things. 'cut off' removes the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification these are ranked groupings, and orders in the broad sense means kinds or classes.

clue.text: Sergeant detailed to turn out gets mad

indicators.note: to turn out the remaining letters means to rearrange them
de-tailed, the sergeant loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An army sergeant ordered to parade gets furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' (read as de-tailed) drops the T from SERGEANT, leaving SERGEAN; 'to turn out' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Makes someone furious is a synonym; mad here is the American sense of angry.

clue.text: Mediterranean city turned upside down to accommodate single lady

indicators.note: the city is to accommodate the single, holding it inside
in a down entry, turned upside down means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Acre is a port city on Israel's Mediterranean coast
single is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A coastal city flipped on its head to house an unmarried woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' puts I inside ACRE to make ACIRE; 'turned upside down' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name stands for a lady.

clue.text: Prince has a thing about the Spanish

indicators.note: the phrase a thing goes about, around, the Spanish article

parts.note: taken as written
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A royal heir has some attachment to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EL inside ATHING, after ATH.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Saxon prince or lord of royal blood bore this title.

clue.text: Unfaithfulness of a grown-up on the end of private line

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult

indicators.note: the end of the word private is its final letter

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A tale of marital betrayal by an adult on a confidential phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes E from 'private'; RY is a standard abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital infidelity is the breaking of faithfulness to a spouse.

clue.text: Frenzied Mawlawi going round in circles — fuel is hard to find

parts.note: whirling is spinning round and round
DERV is British diesel fuel for road vehicles
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Sufi spins dizzily while complaining that fuel is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel road fuel. 'Mawlawi' is the Persian name of the Mevlevi order whose members spin in worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Mevlevi Sufis worship by spinning ecstatically, so a frenzied member of that order is one.

clue.text: Original estate holds right to a court record

indicators.note: the rearranged estate holds the abbreviation inside it
original as in novel, new: the letters of estate take a fresh order

explanation.surface: The first property contains a legal entitlement to a court document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' rearranges the estate's letters to ESTEAT, and 'holds' places R inside that after its third letter. 'Original' works as an anagram signal in the sense of new or novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English law an estreat was a true copy of a fine or recognizance taken from the court rolls.

clue.text: One of a couple liable to be removed by a keeper

definitions.text: One of a couple liable to be removed by a keeper

parts.words: One of a couple liable to be removed by a keeper
parts.note: reads like a lodger evicted by a landlord, but describes one of the two small crosspieces on cricket stumps that a wicketkeeper knocks off

explanation.surface: One of a pair of tenants is at risk of eviction by a landlord or zookeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, two bails rest on the stumps; the one on the leg side can be knocked off by the wicketkeeper to run out or stump a batsman. The phrase also means running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the two crosspieces atop cricket stumps, the leg-side one is a pair member a wicketkeeper may dislodge.

clue.text: Where the highwayman demanded your money?

definitions.text: Where the highwayman demanded your money?

parts.words: Where the highwayman demanded your money?
parts.note: suggests a robber's ambush spot, but means the barrier on a road where a charge for using the highway was collected

explanation.surface: A question about where a mounted robber held up travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: A highwayman is literally anyone of the highway; the turnpike keeper also demanded money from travellers, legally.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike barrier where travellers paid for using the road is where money was demanded.

clue.text: Admirer of beauty scoffed about these resorts

indicators.note: the eaten word goes about, around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: scoffed means ate greedily

indicators.note: re-sorts, the letters of these are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A lover of beauty mocked these holiday towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' (read as re-sorts) rearranges the five letters to ESTHE, which 'about' places within the word for scoffed, after its first letter. The holiday-towns reading of 'resorts' is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to art and beauty is an admirer of the beautiful.

clue.text: Old form of chair lift

parts.note: suggests a ski-slope chair lift, but means an enclosed seat that bearers once carried on poles

explanation.surface: A historical note on early ski-slope chair lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The enclosed seat carried by two bearers was a way of lifting a person in a chair, long before ski lifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The covered chair on poles, borne by two carriers, was an early way to be lifted and transported.

clue.text: Make up one's mind to settle

definitions.meaning: to fix or decide a matter conclusively

explanation.surface: Two phrases for reaching a firm decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to resolve or decide: an intransitive decision and a transitive fixing of a question.

clue.text: An unlikely bet, putting money on ghost being cast out

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound, so money
taken as written

indicators.note: cast out as in thrown into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes cash on a spirit being exorcised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cast out' rearranges the spirit's letters to GSHOT; 'putting money on' reads as a wager, but just sets L before ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager with poor odds of winning is an outsider's chance.

clue.text: More mature sample of alcohol derivative

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A riper specimen taken from a chemical product of alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Being further on in years is being more grown up.

clue.text: Right country church for a love story

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tale of finding the ideal country church for a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of passion and courtship is the sense of this literary genre.

clue.text: Tinker makes a profit, the cunning fellow

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in the induction to Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
boots is an archaic verb meaning profits or avails

explanation.surface: A travelling pot-mender turns a profit, being a crafty sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinker was a travelling mender of pots; Sly is Shakespeare's tinker. 'It boots' (it profits) is an old idiom, as in 'to boot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, crafty person is jocularly called by this old nickname.

clue.text: Old-fashioned company — one in Coventry

parts.note: out of date, out of fashion, is out
a cast is a company of actors

explanation.surface: An old-style theatre troupe performing in the English city of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'send someone to Coventry' is a British idiom for ostracising them, refusing to speak to them; Coventry is a Midlands city.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sent to Coventry is shunned, a pariah rejected by the group.

clue.text: He makes deliveries in Anglo-French waters

parts.note: the English word for waters is sea
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A man delivers goods in the Channel between England and France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' sounds like post; it is cricket balls. A seamer is a bowler who makes the ball deviate off the seam.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler delivers the ball, and a seam bowler is one type.

clue.text: Repellent old woman holding mass of dough has to move clumsily

annotationWithheld.clue: Repellent old woman holding mass of dough has to move clumsily

clue.text: Not rich, keeping a married mistress

indicators.note: the thin word is keeping the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: not rich, as in meagre food, is lean

explanation.surface: A man of modest means supports a wedded lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts M inside the word for not rich, after its second letter. 'Leman' is an archaic word, common in old ballads.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a lover or sweetheart, often an illicit one.

clue.text: Camp in small cottage by lake

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Camping in a tiny cottage beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like a tent site; it is a faction, as in rival camps.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit clique or faction sharing views is a camp.

clue.text: Start to cram old ship with freight

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Begin to pack an ancient vessel with goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes C from 'cram'; the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by a ship are its load.

clue.text: Philanthropy? It's part of a fallible heresy!

indicators.note: is part of says the pronoun sits within the run of the other pieces

parts.note: to err is human, so human means fallible
Arianism was the early Christian heresy denying Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: Is charity a flawed form of heterodox belief?
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's part of' (it is part of) places IT inside the run of the other two pieces. 'To err is human' is the proverb behind fallible; Arius's teaching was condemned at Nicaea.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern for human welfare and charitable action is the same as love of mankind.

clue.text: The currency is not hard

definitions.meaning: legal ... is the money in circulation
soft, easily chewed, as of meat

explanation.surface: A remark that the money in circulation is soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that must be accepted is legal currency; the other sense is soft or delicate.

clue.text: Fear to go rambling without this

definitions.text: Fear to go rambling without this

indicators.note: rambling as in wandering aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A hiker dreads setting off on a walk without their boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' rearranges FEAR TO GO, and the whole clue describes what a walker would not leave home without.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots and shoes are what a walker needs on a hike.
